## Aim and objectives

The aim of this study is to comparatively evaluate the anti-trypanosomal activity
of methanolic extracts of the leaves, stem bark, roots and seeds of
*Azadirachta indica* and *Moringa oleifera* against *Trypanosoma congolense*
and *T. evansi* (thesis §1.8.1).

Specific objectives (§1.8.2): (i) methanolic extraction; (ii) phytochemical
identification/characterisation; (iii) in-vitro motility dose–response at 100,
10, 0.5, 0.01 and 0.005 mg/ml against both parasites; (iv) in-vivo infectivity
in albino mice (body weight, parasitaemia, PCV); (v) comparative efficacy and
superior agent. Objectives i–ii are laboratory procedures reported
descriptively; this report covers the statistical analysis for iii–v.

## Data and design

Source data are group means of n = 3 mice per group, parsed from Sheet 2 of the
study workbook into tidy CSVs (`analysis/data/`, builder
`analysis/R/01_build_datasets.R`). Within any plant × part × parasite block
each of the 7 groups is therefore n = 1 (descriptive only). The analytical
unit is the **block (N = 16; 8 per plant, 8 per parasite)**; plant contrasts
use 8 part × parasite pairs, parasite contrasts 8 plant × part pairs.
Treatments are labelled Negative Control / Positive Control exactly as in the
source (identities and doses not stated in Sheet 2); the Positive Control
serves as assay-validity reference only.

## Endpoints

- **Parasitaemia (LEV 0–5 ordinal):** primary = **AUC** (death-censored
  trapezoidal sum over observed days, reported with mortality); supporting =
  peak LEV, clearance day, day-40 status. Day-40 LEV alone is degenerate
  (0/112 groups positive at day 40: 68 zeros, 44 dead; positivity peaks ~30%
  around days 9–14) and is not used as a primary endpoint.
- **Motility (binary +/−):** time-to-immobilisation (TTI), % motile at t = 120,
  mean proportion motile. Source key: `+ Active motility; − No motility`
  (`+-` undefined → NA, 2 cells).
- **Weight / PCV:** Δ = Post-Infection − Pre-Infection, with
  literature-standard flags — anemia: Post PCV < 35% or ≥ 25% relative drop
  (severe: < 30% or ≥ 40%; Noyes et al. 2009; Naessens et al. 2005; Gitonga et
  al. 2017); weight toxicity signal: ≥ 10% loss (severe: ≥ 20%, the standard
  humane-endpoint range).
- Raw LEV values above the 0–5 scale (42 cells: 41 decimals 5.01–5.3, one
  LEV = 6) were capped to 5 with the pre-cap value preserved (`lev_raw`) and
  flagged. Missing in-vivo values are treated as animal death (adopted
  convention — Sheet 2 never states it; never imputed).

## Statistical methods

All tests are rank-based (LEV ordinal, N small): Friedman test blocked by
block for dose trends with pooled Spearman ρ for log10(concentration);
paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (exact) for dose-vs-Negative-Control and for
plant/parasite contrasts, with matched-pairs rank-biserial effect size
(Cliff's delta family; |r| ≥ 0.11/0.28/0.43 small/medium/large per Vargha &
Delaney 2000) and Hodges–Lehmann median difference with 95% CI; Holm
adjustment within each dose-vs-control family. Per-block trend tests at n = 1
have no power and pooled trend tests would break independence, so only the
blocked Friedman is reported as inference. Significance at p < 0.05;
p-values are supplementary to effect sizes. Analysis script:
`analysis/R/02_analysis.R` (statistics only, no ML).

## Results — dose response (objective iii–iv)

Mean AUC falls monotonically with concentration for *T. evansi* and
approximately for *T. congolense* (@fig-dose).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dose
#| tbl-cap: Dose-response tests on parasitaemia AUC (Friedman blocked by block; Spearman on log10 dose).
k("dose_response.csv")
```

![Mean AUC vs log10(concentration) by parasite](`r file.path(fig_dir, "auc_dose_response.png")`){#fig-dose}

## Results — doses vs Negative Control

*T. evansi*: 100, 10 and 0.5 mg/ml all beat the control in every block
(W = 0, exact p = 0.008, Holm 0.039; HL ≈ −50/−50/−44 AUC-days). Lower doses
are weaker (Holm 0.078). *T. congolense*: only 100 mg/ml is suggestive
(p = 0.014, Holm 0.071) — not significant after correction.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-vsnc
#| tbl-cap: Each dose vs Negative Control on AUC (paired Wilcoxon by block; Holm per parasite).
k("dose_vs_nc_auc.csv")
```

## Results — plant superiority (objective v)

No evidence of a difference between *A. indica* and *M. oleifera*: paired
W = 14, exact p = 1.0, HL ≈ 0.3 AUC-days, 95% CI (−14.7, +20.5); motility
paired p = 0.15. Pairs scatter on both sides of identity (@fig-paired), so
at N = 8 pairs the data cannot support a superiority claim.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-superiority
#| tbl-cap: Plant superiority contrasts (8 pairs each).
k("plant_superiority.csv")
k("plant_superiority_motility.csv")
```

![Paired block-mean AUC: A. indica vs M. oleifera](`r file.path(fig_dir, "plant_paired_auc.png")`){#fig-paired}

## Results — parasite contrast; weight and PCV

No parasite difference in AUC (p = 0.46). Weight and PCV deltas show no
plant or parasite signals (all p ≥ 0.15); flags below are descriptive.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-other
#| tbl-cap: Parasite, weight and PCV contrasts.
k("parasite_comparison.csv")
k("weight_tests.csv")
k("pcv_tests.csv")
```

## Limitations

1. Each CSV row is a mean of n = 3 mice; no within-group variance survives,
   so all inference is at N = 16 blocks (8 per contrast) — power is low and
   confidence intervals are wide; descriptive patterns carry the weight.
2. Control identities/doses are unknown in the source; Positive Control is a
   validity reference, not a non-inferiority comparator.
3. Death-censored AUC favours early-death groups numerically; every AUC is
   therefore reported alongside mortality — low AUC with high mortality reads
   as failure, not efficacy.
4. NA = death is an adopted convention (Sheet 2 never states it); confirm
   against the thesis animal records if possible.
